title: Emerald Waypoint private deploy call notes and ops sketch
body:
High-level summary: call with Emerald Waypoint (infra + security leads) on 2026-03-12 11:00 PST. Purpose: evaluate feasibility of an air-gapped/private deployment in their colo for a customer-support chat assistant and an internal vector search pipeline. They require strict data residency, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and signed/artifact verification. Notes below are raw and intended for handoff to eng-private-deployments and SRE.

Attendees: Priya (Redwood RE), Marco (solutions), Danielle (CS), Ethan (SE) — Emerald: Nora (infra lead), Samir (ML infra), Laila (security)

Key asks & constraints:
- No outbound internet from model hosts. Control-plane can route through a customer-managed jumpbox for approved operations. No telemetry to Redwood by default.
- Mandatory customer-managed KMS (Thales Luna or AWS CloudHSM). Key rotation cadence enforced by customer; we must not hold unencrypted model keys.
- Initial model scope: Llama-3-13B (open) + an internal fine-tuned 7B variant. They want quantized artifacts where possible to conserve GPU memory.
- Performance targets: sustain 12 concurrent interactive chat sessions with p95/p99 token latencies ideally under 350ms. Embedding throughput target ~20 req/s for short docs.
- Audit/log residency: all logs/audits must remain in their VPC; optional selective export to their S3 is acceptable. No Redwood-hosted metric ingestion.

Technical gotchas surfaced:
- Image acceptance policy: colo requires signed OCI images from a registry mirror. Need an offline bundle option plus an auditable signing & verification process (SBOM required).
- Kernel/driver mismatch risk: their hosts run an older RHEL kernel; GPUs are A100-40GB but driver/CUDA may be incompatible. Preflight must detect driver mismatch; otherwise we need a vendor driver shim or alternative execution path.
- HSM latency: on-prem HSMs add non-trivial latency to cryptographic ops. Plan to benchmark key unwrap/sign latencies; consider async token caching to avoid per-request stalls.
- Persistent KV cache preference: they prefer NFS-backed TTL storage. Warn about NFS concurrency and suggest local fallback for hot KV shards.
- Artifact distribution: they prefer rsync from a Redwood staging mirror via jumpbox. Provide GPG-signed artifact bundles + sha256 manifest.
- Quant runtime: confirm our runtime supports INT8 quant paths on A100; if not, provide fp16 fallback with documented perf delta.

Rough capacity sketch (initial):
- Llama-3-13B INT8 on A100: estimate ~1.2k tokens/s per GPU. For peak concurrency (12 sessions, burst to 40 t/s per convo), suggest 3 GPUs (2 active + 1 spare) in first release.
- Embedding flow: small GPU or CPU path for short-doc embeddings at ~20 req/s; keep index on 80GB SSD, recommend separate node for heavy index work.
- Storage: 1TB local NVMe per node for model cache; 2TB NFS for persistent KV/storage.
- Nodes: recommend 3x A100-40GB nodes, use k8s node selectors/taints to isolate workload.

Ops & integration questions for ENG/SRE:
1) HSM integration: can our private control plane use customer HSMs for disk encryption and token signing without exposing keys? Impact on control plane architecture?
2) Offline image bundles: who generates and rotates signed bundles? Need a documented flow and automation for bundle creation.
3) Telemetry: can we support local-only observability with optional metrics export to customer S3? What retention and disk sizing guidance can we give?
4) Artifact signing: can our CI produce GPG-signed manifests and consistent sha256 sums for multi-shard model artifacts?
5) Persistent KV on NFS: does the runtime safely handle NFS-backed caches; if not, what's the recommended lock/fallback pattern?

Security team concerns:
- Complete SBOM and signed provenance required for any container or artifact.
- Principle of least privilege for service accounts; customer will not accept broad-scoped tokens on nodes.
- Audit logs must include per-request model version, prompt hash (hashed client-side), and fallback decision metadata.

Commercial / timeline notes:
- Pricing ask: Emerald requested per-GPU monthly blended cost and rough reserved vs burst modeling. Danielle to send templated cost worksheet.
- Pilot: requested 6-week pilot (2 weeks integration + 4 weeks ops smoke tests).

Immediate next steps (owners and target dates):
- Priya: produce a 1-page air-gapped deployment checklist for Emerald (image signing, artifact mirroring, preflight checks, HSM notes). Due 2026-03-14.
- Marco: run quick INT8 perf tests on A100 with current runtime and report numbers. Due 2026-03-18.
- Danielle: deliver pricing worksheet + pilot contract draft to Emerald by 2026-03-15.
- Ethan: open Jira epic ENG-2297 to capture infra work, estimate tasks (image bundles, preflight, KMS integration). Due 2026-03-13.
- SRE/Infra: prototype offline artifact delivery and verification script (GPG + sha256) to hand to customer.

Questions for Emerald (follow-up):
- Would they accept an initial temporary outbound-only egress for first-time model pulls via private peering? This simplifies sync.
- Confirm HSM vendor (Thales vs AWS CloudHSM) so we can run vendor-specific latency tests.
- Clarify maintenance window preferences and patch cadence for kernel/driver updates.

Handoff notes: make the customer-facing checklist concise, include a small appendix with expected perf numbers (once Marco has them), clear SBOM instructions, and an annotated artifact delivery playbook. Keep the first pilot narrow: enable chat assistant + embeddings only, expand after ops baseline confirmed.
